prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs (budget, timing, warranty, brand preference, home size). A safe next step: tell me your ZIP code and any preferences (budget range, preferred brands, whether you need financing or same‑day service) and I’ll narrow good local options and what to ask them. 

Meanwhile, here’s how to find the best HVAC company in Atlanta and what to ask so you get a great AC replacement:

What to require from any contractor
- Current license and proof of insurance (liability + workers’ comp).  
- NATE‑certified technicians (shows professional training).  
- Manufacturer training/authorization if you want a branded system warranty.  
- Written, itemized estimate (equipment, labor, permits, disposal).  
- Clear warranty: equipment (manufacturer) and labor (installer).  
- Agree to pull required permits and perform final system checkout/balancing.

Where to find reputable contractors
- Google and Yelp (look at recent reviews and responses to complaints).  
- Angi / HomeAdvisor for screened pros.  
- Better Business Bureau for complaint history.  
- Local Facebook community groups or Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals.

Questions to ask when you call/get a quote
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide license number?  
- How many years have you replaced systems in this ZIP? Any references?  
- What size/SEER rating would you recommend and why? Will you do a load calculation (Manual J)?  
- Is the equipment matched (air handler and condenser)? Who is the manufacturer and model?  
- What’s included in labor warranty and how long? Any extended maintenance plan?  
- Do you include permit fees, disposal of old unit, and electrical/work required?  
- Estimated total cost and timeline. Any financing or rebates available?

Red flags to avoid
- Vague written estimates or high-pressure “today‑only” deals.  
- No load calculation (they should size the system to your home).  
- Unwillingness to show license/insurance or references.  
- Significantly lower price than everyone else without explanation.

Price and value guidance
- Get at least 3 written quotes and compare system SEER, brand, installation details, and warranty — not just price.  
- Consider long‑term energy savings (higher SEER). A cheaper install with poor workmanship can cost more in the long run.

If you want, give me your ZIP code and any preferences and I’ll produce a short list of highly rated Atlanta HVAC companies and what to ask each one — or paste any quotes you’ve received and I’ll help you compare them.
